## Analysis

**Affected Plant Part & Visual Features:**
- The plant shows multiple tillers (shoots) emerging from the base
- Leaves are thin, narrow, and elongated
- The plant has a distinctly bushy, grass-like appearance
- Leaves appear pale yellow to chlorotic (lacking green color)
- Severely reduced internode length (compressed internodes)
- Overall stunted, clumpy growth pattern
- No visible leaf spotting, necrosis patterns, or mosaic patterns

**Symptom Matching:**

The image shows the classic presentation of **Grassy_Shoot** disease:
- ✓ Numerous tillers growing from the base
- ✓ Pale yellow to chlorotic, thin and narrow leaves
- ✓ Grass-like bushy appearance due to premature, continuous tillering
- ✓ Severely reduced internode length creating compressed appearance
- ✓ Overall stunted, clumpy growth

This distinctly rules out other candidates:
- Yellow_Leaf would show specific midrib necrosis/yellowing patterns
- Mosaic viruses (SCMV, SCSMV) would show striping or mosaic patterns
- Leaf_Scald would show the white pencil-line symptom
- Pokkah_Boeng would show twisted/knife-cut characteristics
